games.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
notes: Steam Special Edition (Windows build, app 489830) only; the 2011 original and Skyrim VR are not covered.
Steam Play opens the Skyrim launcher first; its auto-detected preset can pick a resolution the Mac cannot hold: choose a modest preset once.
Reported on CrossOver 25.1.1 / M4 Pro: crash after the Bethesda logo, with or without SKSE (CodeWeavers forum). Current CrossOver rating is Runs Great via DXMT.
Some mods and ENB presets bind Home/End/Insert keys a Mac keyboard lacks: remap them in the mod .ini files.
Very large mod lists have crashed at random under Wine (memory); add mods in small steps and keep a save.
Mods install into the prefix exactly as on Windows (Data folder, SKSE next to SkyrimSE.exe).

games.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
notes: DX11 mode only: Play launches bin/x64/witcher3.exe directly. Through Steam the REDlauncher opens: pick "DirectX 11" in its dropdown (or set "fallback": "DirectX 11" in launcher-configuration.json and add --launcher-skip, which otherwise falls back to DX12).
FSR and other next-gen DX12-only features are not available in DX11 mode.
Under DXVK some enemies (sirens) were invisible (Stream Output); not confirmed either way under DXMT.
About 80 GB free disk for the Windows build in the prefix.
Without a middle mouse button, bind "Use Quick Access Item" to a spare key (Options > Key Bindings).

games.name: Heroes of Might and Magic III
notes: Needs Heroes III Complete Edition (GOG) or Shadow of Death data. The GOG offline backup installer (.exe + .bin) is imported by the VCMI launcher on first start.
The Steam HD Edition alone is not enough: VCMI can only add its HD graphics on top of a Complete/SoD install.
Data lives in ~/Library/Application Support/vcmi/ (Data, Maps, Mp3), VCMI's own folder, not the SIGF ports folder.
VCMI is an open-source reimplementation of the engine (GPL-2.0-or-later), not the original exe.
Engine download is a DMG: it is mounted and VCMI.app copied out.

games.name: Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour
notes: Needs the Steam Windows build of Zero Hour (app 2732960): Steam for Mac offers no Install button, so the files come from Windows Steam (or SteamCMD forced to the Windows platform).
Copy the whole game folder, ZH_Generals/ included: it holds the base Generals archives (Textures.big, Generals.big); without them units and terrain render magenta.
run.sh reads the data from CNC_GENERALS_ZH_PATH (default ~/GeneralsX/GeneralsZH) and the base game from CNC_GENERALS_PATH or ZH_Generals/.
GeneralsX reaches campaigns and skirmish on Apple Silicon (project test matrix: macOS 26, Working). Online play uses GeneralsOnline, cross-platform, not EA servers.
The app bundle is unsigned upstream.

games.name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
notes: Native Apple Silicon build in Mac Steam, free for existing Steam owners; no Wine.
Online skirmish is against other Mac players (no cross-play with PC announced).

games.name: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

config.text:
data="{data}/Data Files"
fallback-archive=Morrowind.bsa
fallback-archive=Tribunal.bsa
fallback-archive=Bloodmoon.bsa
content=Morrowind.esm
content=Tribunal.esm
content=Bloodmoon.esm

notes: Uses the Data Files folder of the Steam Windows GOTY edition (Morrowind, Tribunal, Bloodmoon).
OpenMW is an open-source reimplementation of the engine, not the original exe; Morrowind Code Patch and MGE XE do not apply.
Settings, mod list and load order live in ~/Library/Preferences/openmw/openmw.cfg; an existing file there is kept as is.
Saves go to ~/Library/Application Support/openmw/saves.
Non-English editions may need encoding=win1250 (Polish/Czech) or win1251 (Russian) in openmw.cfg.
The macOS build needs macOS 14.8 or newer and an Apple Silicon Mac.

games.name: RollerCoaster Tycoon 2
notes: Uses the whole Steam Windows install of RCT2 Triple Thrill Pack (about 300 MB).
OpenRCT2 is an open-source re-implementation; old RCT2 saves and scenarios load, and multiplayer works with other OpenRCT2 players.
OpenRCT2 settings and saves live in ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRCT2.
The OpenRCT2 app is not code signed upstream.

games.name: RollerCoaster Tycoon Classic
notes: RCT Classic has its own Mac version on Steam: install it with Steam for Mac, OpenRCT2 then reads its data in place.
You can also just play the Mac version from Steam; OpenRCT2 adds native Apple Silicon, big screens and multiplayer.
Only the default Steam library folder is found; for another library, set the RCT2 path in OpenRCT2 options.

games.name: Diablo + Hellfire
notes: Pick the folder that holds DIABDAT.MPQ: a Windows install of GOG Diablo + Hellfire, or the original CD.
The GOG offline installer is a Windows .exe: install it on a PC (or extract it with innoextract) to get the .mpq files.
Add hellfire.mpq, hfmonk.mpq, hfmusic.mpq and hfvoice.mpq to play Hellfire.
DevilutionX is a source port of Diablo; saves and diablo.ini live in ~/Library/Application Support/diasurgical/devilution.

games.name: Fallout
notes: Uses the whole Steam Windows install of Fallout (master.dat, critter.dat, data/).
Game files and saves (data/SAVEGAME) sit next to the engine app: removing the engine removes the saves, back them up first.
Fallout CE is a re-implementation of the original engine with quality-of-life fixes; sfall-based mods are only partly supported.
If music is silent, set music_path1 in fallout.cfg to the folder that holds the .ACM files (data/sound/music/).

games.name: Fallout 2
notes: Uses the whole Steam Windows install of Fallout 2 (master.dat, critter.dat, patch000.dat, data/).
Game files and saves (data/SAVEGAME) sit next to the engine app: removing the engine removes the saves, back them up first.
Window size: f2_res.ini (SCR_WIDTH, SCR_HEIGHT, WINDOWED) in the same folder.
Fallout 2 CE includes part of sfall; big mods such as Restoration Project or Fallout Et Tu may not run fully.

games.name: DOOM + DOOM II
notes: Uses the Steam Windows DOOM + DOOM II (2024 release): UZDoom lists DOOM, DOOM II, TNT and Plutonia (KEX and original DOS versions) at start.
Final DOOM (2290) and DOOM II (2300) are no longer sold separately; their content is in DOOM + DOOM II.
UZDoom is a GZDoom-based source port: the KEX online modes and in-game mod browser are not available; classic WAD/PK3 mods work.
If you edited UZDoom's IWAD search paths in its .ini yourself, keep $DOOMWADPATH in them.

games.name: Heretic + Hexen
notes: Uses the original DOS game data shipped inside the Steam Windows Heretic + Hexen (2025); pick Heretic, Hexen or Deathkings at start.
The new Nightdive episodes (KEX content) are not playable in UZDoom.
Owners of the old Steam Heretic (2390) or Hexen (2360) only: these are not covered by this recipe yet.

games.name: Duke Nukem 3D: 20th Anniversary World Tour
notes: Uses the Steam Windows 20th Anniversary World Tour install, including Episode 5.
Raze plays the classic game; the 20th Anniversary extras (developer commentary, its renderer modes) are not available.

games.name: Blood
notes: For owners of Blood: Fresh Supply on Steam (no longer sold, still downloadable). Cryptic Passage is in addons/ and found by Raze.
Blood: Refreshed Supply (2025) is not supported by this recipe: Raze 1.11.0 predates it.
Raze is a source port of the Build engine games; Fresh Supply's own online and enhanced options are not available.

games.name: Shadow Warrior Classic
notes: Shadow Warrior Classic (1997) is free on Steam and has a Mac version: install it with Steam for Mac, Raze finds it.
Pick Shadow Warrior in Raze's game list on start (it lists every Build game it found).
Wanton Destruction and Twin Dragon come with Shadow Warrior Classic Redux (225160), whose Mac files Raze does not look for.

games.name: PowerSlave
notes: PowerSlave (DOS Classic Edition) has a Mac version on Steam: install it with Steam for Mac, Raze finds it.
Pick PowerSlave in Raze's game list on start.
PowerSlave Exhumed (the 2022 Nightdive remaster) is not covered.

games.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert (OpenRA)
notes: OpenRA is a free open-source reimplementation (GPL-3.0); it does not run the original exe and plays differently (modern RTS controls, balance).
No purchase needed: on first start OpenRA's content installer downloads the freeware Red Alert files EA released in 2008 (about 100 MB) into ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA/Content/ra.
Music and the full campaign videos come from an original disc or the C&C Remastered Collection; the freeware package covers the playable game.
Online multiplayer uses OpenRA's own server browser, cross-platform with other OpenRA players.

games.name: Command & Conquer: Tiberian Dawn (OpenRA)
notes: OpenRA is a free open-source reimplementation (GPL-3.0) of the 1995 Command & Conquer, not the original exe.
No purchase needed: the content installer downloads the freeware C&C files (released by EA in 2007) into ~/Library/Application Support/OpenRA/Content/cnc on first start.
Online multiplayer uses OpenRA's own server browser, cross-platform with other OpenRA players.

games.name: Tomb Raider II (TRX)
notes: TRX is an open-source engine for the original Tomb Raider games (GPL-3.0), with widescreen, modern controls and many fixes.
Needs the Steam Windows release (app 225300): its data and fmv folders are copied into the engine.
Golden Mask (expansion) is bundled free by TRX: pick it in the game's passport.
The Steam release has no CD music; TRX's Windows installer offers a separate music download that this recipe does not fetch, so expect silence where music would play.
Uses TRX's older flat data layout (top-level data/ and fmv/), which TRX still reads but no longer documents.

games.name: Tomb Raider (TRX)
notes: Pick a folder that holds the game's DATA and FMV folders (and MUSIC if you have the track files).
Steam (app 224960) and GOG ship Tomb Raider I as a CD image (GAME.DAT / GAME.GOG): the files must be extracted from that image first; SIGF cannot do it yet.
Unfinished Business is bundled free by TRX: pick it in the game's passport.
Uses TRX's older flat data layout (top-level data/ and fmv/), which TRX still reads but no longer documents.

games.name: Caesar III (Julius)
notes: Julius is an open-source re-creation of Caesar III (AGPL-3.0) with the same game logic; saves are compatible with the original.
Needs the Steam Windows release (app 517790): the whole game folder is copied, and Julius saves into that copy.
Julius needs the patched game (v1.0.1); if it says the files are older, apply the official patch to the Windows install first.
Adds widescreen and windowed play; Julius is the vanilla-rules engine (Augustus would change gameplay).

games.name: FreeSpace 2 (FSO)
notes: FreeSpace 2 Open is the community-maintained engine built from Volition's source release (non-commercial licence).
Needs the Steam Windows release (app 273620): the retail .vp archives (and the data folders with movies, when present) are copied next to the engine, which reads them from its working folder.
Plays the retail game as shipped; the MediaVPs graphics upgrade and Knossos mod launcher are not part of this recipe.
Pilots and settings are kept in ~/Library/Application Support/HardLightProductions/FreeSpaceOpen.

games.name: Gothic II: Gold Edition (OpenGothic)
notes: OpenGothic is an open-source engine (MIT) for Gothic II: Night of the Raven, rendering through Metal.

Needs the Steam Windows release (app 39510, Gold Edition = Gothic II + Night of the Raven): Data and _work are copied to ~/Library/Application Support/OpenGothic, where OpenGothic finds them by itself; saves go there too.
Modern renderer: original graphics settings do not apply; ray tracing is off on integrated GPUs.
Mods that need the original exe or Union/Ninja plugins do not work; script-only mods can be started with -game:<mod>.ini.

games.name: Gothic (OpenGothic)
notes: OpenGothic (MIT) mainly targets Gothic II; Gothic 1 runs with -g1 but is less polished: expect missing details and occasional script bugs.
Needs the Steam Windows release (app 65540, "Gothic 1 Classic"), not the Gothic 1 Remake.
Saves are written next to the OpenGothic engine (removing the engine removes them).

games.name: Theme Hospital (CorsixTH)
notes: CorsixTH is an open-source re-creation of Theme Hospital (MIT) with widescreen, higher resolutions and fixes.
Theme Hospital is not on Steam: pick the installed folder of your copy (GOG or the original CD install) that holds Data, Levels and QData.
Sound and Anims are optional: without them the game is silent and skips movies.
Settings changed in game are kept (config.txt next to the copied data).

games.name: Descent 3 (open source)
notes: Descent 3 open source (GPL-3.0, released by the original developers) running the Steam Windows data (app 273590).
Steam also lists an old Mac build of Descent 3; this recipe uses the Windows files on purpose: the project notes that movies only work with them.
Data must be game version 1.4 (the Steam release is).
Pilots and saves are written next to the engine (removing the engine removes them).

games.name: Chris Sawyer's Locomotion (OpenLoco)
notes: OpenLoco is an open-source re-implementation of Locomotion (MIT), with bug fixes and higher resolutions.
Needs the Steam Windows release (app 356430): Data, ObjData and Scenarios are copied.
Saves, settings and screenshots are in ~/Library/Application Support/OpenLoco.
OpenLoco multiplayer is experimental.

games.name: Jagged Alliance 2 (Stracciatella)
notes: JA2 Stracciatella is an open-source port of the released JA2 source (non-commercial licence), with higher resolutions and fixes.
Needs the Steam Windows release of Jagged Alliance 2 Gold (app 1620): its Data folder is copied.
Jagged Alliance 2 Classic (app 545210) already has a Mac build on Steam; its data should work too but this recipe uses Gold.
English data assumed; other languages need -resversion (GERMAN, FRENCH, ...).
Unfinished Business and Wildfire are not covered by this recipe.

games.name: Carmageddon (dethrace)
notes: dethrace is a reverse-engineered open-source Carmageddon engine (non-commercial use only).
Needs the Steam Windows release of the Carmageddon Max Pack (app 282010): its CARMA folder is copied.
Plays the original Carmageddon; the Splat Pack expansion is not wired up by this recipe.
A dethrace.ini in ~/Library/Application Support/dethrace overrides the data folder and settings (hires, windowed, 3dfx mode).

games.name: Fallout: New Vegas
notes: Steam Windows build (app 22380). D3D9 through Wine's own renderer (OpenGL), not DXMT.
Steam Play opens the New Vegas launcher first: pick a modest preset once (the auto-detect can pick settings the Mac cannot hold).
Older Macs run it slowly (about 15 fps reported on an M1 Mac mini under CrossOver 21); newer Macs and CrossOver 25 report it running well.
If music or radio is silent, the MP3 decoder (GStreamer) is the usual suspect: say so in the report with the log.
The 4GB Patcher and NVSE install into the game folder as on Windows.

games.name: Fallout 3: Game of the Year Edition
notes: Steam Windows build (app 22370, GFWL already removed by Bethesda). D3D9 through Wine's own renderer, not DXMT.
CodeWeavers reports it may fail to open or run at 10-15 fps on Apple Silicon. Highest risk of this batch.
Crashes or stutter on many-core CPUs: in Documents/My Games/Fallout3/FALLOUT.ini set bUseThreadedAI=1 and add iNumHWThreads=2 (the usual Windows fix, also recommended for Wine).
Steam Play opens the Fallout 3 launcher first: choose a modest preset once.

games.name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Game of the Year Edition
notes: The 2006 game on Steam (app 22330), not Oblivion Remastered. D3D9 through Wine's own renderer.
Steam Play opens the Oblivion launcher first: choose a modest preset once.
Missing music or voices is the most reported problem under CrossOver (it ships an audio override for this game): send the log if it happens.
Mods go into Data as on Windows; OBSE goes next to Oblivion.exe.

games.name: Fallout 4
notes: Steam Windows build (app 377160). CrossOver rates it Runs Well on macOS with DXMT.
An older DXMT showed VATS hit chances at 0% and crashed loading a quicksave; reported fixed in newer DXMT. If VATS reads 0%, say so in the report.
Steam Play opens the Fallout 4 launcher first: choose a modest preset once (Godrays and shadows cost the most on a Mac).
About 35 GB free disk (more with the high-resolution texture pack, which is not worth it on a Mac).

games.name: Kenshi
notes: Steam Windows build (app 233860), 64-bit. Untested on Mac with DXMT: no public report either way.
Kenshi's own launcher opens first: keep the DirectX 11 renderer (not OpenGL), and enable mods there (load order).
Large towns are CPU-heavy on any machine; expect slowdowns there.

games.name: Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord
notes: Single player only: multiplayer needs Easy Anti-Cheat, which does not work under Wine.
CrossOver rates it Limited Functionality: the TaleWorlds launcher (what Steam Play opens) often fails under Wine. Players who got in started the game exe directly.
Reported with DXMT: ground disappearing and stretched objects in some scenes.
The game runs on .NET Framework; Wine Mono stands in for it. If it stops at startup, send the log.
Mods go into Modules as on Windows and are enabled in the launcher.

games.name: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
notes: Reported playable on an M5 MacBook Air with this same Wine 10 + DXMT setup.
Known DXMT 0.80 bug: freezes of many seconds in some scenes (fixed in the next DXMT). Wait it out; it is not a crash.
Mods use Sekiro Mod Engine (a dinput8.dll in the game folder); it may need dinput8 set to native, which this recipe does not do yet.

games.name: Dark Souls: Remastered
notes: Play offline (in-game Network settings: launch in offline mode). Online play under Wine is untested and modified games risk a flag.
Ran at about 60 fps on an M1 under CrossOver (DXVK); not yet confirmed with DXMT.
Texture flicker in Blighttown was reported under CrossOver 22.

games.name: Dark Souls III
notes: Play offline (in-game Network settings: launch in offline mode). Online play under Wine is untested.
Reported around 30 fps at 900p medium on an M1 under CrossOver; brief freezes on fast camera moves.
The in-game graphics menu can lag badly: settings can also be edited in %APPDATA%/DarkSoulsIII/GraphicsConfig.xml inside the prefix.
Start it with Play (through Steam): the exe started on its own restarts through Steam anyway.

games.name: Monster Hunter: World
notes: DirectX 11 only: in graphics_option.ini (game folder) set DirectX12Enable=Off before the first launch, or in Options > Display turn DirectX 12 off.
Older CrossOver reports: black screen, then a freeze at the main menu. One 2024 report ran it in DX11 mode on an M1 Pro. Treat it as experimental.
Co-op goes through Capcom's servers and Steam; it is untested here.
About 50 GB free disk with Iceborne.
